title: Workspace trust dialog gets stuck
body:
### Summary

After updating to version 253e6195 on macOS and using `hx` as my Git core editor, making a commit opens up `hx` alongside a workspace trust dialog. However, I cannot progress past the dialog because my keyboard buttons do nothing in the related terminal tab, when the dialog is open.

### Reproduction Steps

<!-- Ideally provide a key sequence and/or asciinema.org recording. --> 

I tried this:

1. Install version 253e6195 of Helix on macOS.
2. Set `hx` as your Git `core.editor`.
3. Try to make a commit in the macOS terminal.
4. Observe that arrow buttons do nothing in the workspace trust dialog that opens along with the editor.

I expected this to happen: I should be able to actually make a selection in the workspace trust dialog.

Instead, this happened: Kyeboard buttons do nothing in the terminal tab that has the workspace trust dialog open.


### Helix log

The only line from today in the log file is below.
<details><summary>~/.cache/helix/helix.log</summary>

```
2026-03-27T10:49:15.778 helix_view::document [WARN] Error building syntax for '~/.cache/helix/helix.log': configured timeout was exceeded
```

</details>


### Platform

macOS

### Terminal Emulator

Terminal version 2.15 (466)

### Installation Method

source

### Helix Version

helix 25.07.1 (253e6195)

Your terminal probably can't receive any key inputs, for whatever reason. You can set this config option, it will get rid of trust dialog. I don't really think it will fix key inputs (or I don't have any idea what is going on)
```toml
[editor]
insecure = true
````

comments.body:
I took this to the aerc IRC channel and found a workaround and a suggestion that it's due to the Helix terminal parser not resyncing on unexpected input.

(lightly edited) log below (I'm dutchie):

```
  <septante> dutchie: try this: when helix hangs on startup, press esc on your kbd, take a breath, press backslash; voila                                                                         
   <dutchie> ah that works                                                                                                                                                                        
  <septante> ;^)                                                                                                                                                                                  
<rockorager> Oooh
  <septante> dutchie: [...] tell the [maintainers] of helix that their parser [has issues] and won't resync on unexpected input                                           
<rockorager> parser gets stuck waiting for ST but actually got a bel?                                                                                                                             
  <septante> yep,                                                                                                                                                                                 
   <dutchie> interesting                                                                                                                                                                          
<rockorager> septante is the true agi                                                                                                                                                             
<rockorager> Hm. I generally like to use ESC \ as an ST, but I remmeber someone complaining about not using BEL for OSC terminations                                                              
  <septante> vaxis should be fine using bel; both are acceptable i believe; helix should prob check for both;                                                                                     
<rockorager> Yeah the "spec" says ST or BEL can terminate an osc                        
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I was able to fix it with [this change to termina](https://github.com/participant1/termina/commit/45df6438c2183b64d44cde7bb80cc8037a1a8d85) (I tested with aerc, don't know if that fixes macOS terminal), but I don't know if I should send a PR with this change...

It feels kinda clunky, and this is a workaround around broken terminal, so I probably shouldn't bother the maintainers.

One might claim that this is not a bug in the terminal, but in our parser; consider this: [ghostty has to deal with the same problem](https://ghostty.org/docs/vt/concepts/sequences#osc), but they deal with it (IMO) properly: it accepts both OSC terminators, and replies with the one client was using. If your terminal sends `BEL` in response to `ESC \`, I would claim that's a bug in your terminal, and not in our parser.
